title: Fork Where the Model Changes Its Mind: Belief-Shift Branching for Tree-Structured RL
trick: Every few steps ask the model what answer it currently believes (a 9-token suffix, read the next-token distribution) and fork right before the step where that belief jumps most.
framing_stripped: Called belief-shift branching; it is a cheap probe of the model's own answer distribution, differenced across consecutive step boundaries, used as a fork selector.
load_bearing_assumption: A jump in the model's own answer belief marks a consequential step (true in math where only the model's reasoning changes belief; untested where observations arrive from an environment).
weakest_component: No notion of right or wrong: the probe moves when the model changes its mind, not when it moves toward the truth; cannot separate new information from a decision in an agent setting.
regime: Math (AIME) and code (LiveCodeBench-medium); OLMo-3 7B/32B, Qwen3; 10 forks per chain; probe costs ~1% of step compute on math, <5% on code.
information_asymmetry: The model's belief is available at every boundary for free, but the environment's reference (what the belief should move toward) is available at training time and unused.
occupies: Validated placement against Monte Carlo value curves on math; the finding that entropy tracks wording freedom, not outcome (3.6x less flip mass captured).

neighbors.trick: Branch where the ending depends most on the action, per cost, estimated from pilots.
Entropy-placed tree forking on search agents.

theme_fit.why: a validated placement signal and the protocol to validate one

limitations_as_complaints: I cannot tell a belief shift caused by reading a file from one caused by a decision.
No large ablation on candidate-boundary density.
